source: Polu & Sutskever (2020) Generative Language Modeling for Automated Theorem Proving (GPT-f)
finding: First transformer prover for Metamath. A proof checker accepts or rejects every proof, so search runs on a hard pass/fail signal. Some shorter proofs it found were accepted into the main Metamath library.
numbers: Best model closes 56.22% of held-out Metamath proofs vs 21.16% for MetaGen-IL. Pretraining on WebMath: 160m 28.96% (scratch) to 34.79%; 700m 31.58% to 42.56%.
limits: Metamath only; proofs are low level. Adding synthetic proofs at 5% of data hurt.
agent_relevance: The exact checker is why the loop works. Verify (S8) on exact tasks should be a program, not a model opinion (G2, G3).

source: Polu & Sutskever (2020) GPT-f: value function and size
finding: Training a value function on the prover's own search statements helps. Policy plus value beats policy alone.
numbers: 700m policy only 42.56%/42.23%/43.15% across search budgets; policy+value 44.59%/47.21%. 160m: 34.79% to 39.27%/40.70%.
limits: Gains are a few points; search cost not normalised in this summary.
agent_relevance: A learned scorer on top of a hard checker can rank branches, but the checker still decides.

source: Lample et al. (2022) HyperTree Proof Search for Neural Theorem Proving
finding: AlphaZero-style search over proof hypertrees plus online training on unproved theorems. Retraining on search results lifts accuracy.
numbers: Metamath held-out: 65.4% (vs 56.5% GPT-f), 82.6% after online training. miniF2F-curriculum in Lean: 31% to 42%.
limits: Compute heavy; online training is training, which our scaffold forbids.
agent_relevance: Backtracking tree search with a hard verifier is the strong baseline; borrow the search shape without the training.

source: Jiang et al. (2023) Draft, Sketch, and Prove (DSP)
finding: LLM writes an informal proof, turns it into a formal sketch with open gaps, and an off-the-shelf prover fills the gaps. Roughly doubles the base prover on miniF2F with Isabelle.
numbers: miniF2F-test: Sledgehammer+heuristics 20.9% to DSP 39.3% (human informal proofs) or 37.7% (Minerva 62B). Valid: 42.6% (human). 200 of 488 problems solved.
limits: Informal proof source mattered little: Minerva 540B 38.9%, 8B 36.5%. Isabelle only; competition set.
agent_relevance: This is the subgoal-library pattern: plan in prose, state subgoals in checkable form, let a simple prover close each one.

finding: Removing in-line comments that copy the informal proof into the sketch hurt. The informal draft and the automated prover each carried weight.
numbers: No in-line comments: -4.9 (valid) and -2.8 (test) points vs DSP with human proofs.
limits: One benchmark; single run per cell.
agent_relevance: Keep the prose plan attached to each formal subgoal so a checker failure traces back to a plan step (G2).

source: Wu et al. (2022) Autoformalization with Large Language Models
finding: Few-shot LLMs can translate competition problems into formal statements. Training a prover on those synthetic statements raised its miniF2F score.
numbers: 25.3% of problems translated perfectly into Isabelle/HOL; miniF2F proof rate 29.6% to 35.2%.
limits: About three quarters of translations were wrong or partial; a misformalized statement can be proved while the real problem is not.
agent_relevance: Translation into formal language is the weak link. Check the formal statement against the original (G3).

source: Yang et al. (2023) LeanDojo and ReProver
finding: Open Lean toolkit and a retrieval-augmented prover. Retrieval of premises helped. The earlier tool lean-gym wrongly rejected many correct human proofs.
numbers: LeanDojo benchmark Pass@1: ReProver 51.2%, no retrieval 47.6%, GPT-4 zero-shot 29.0%. miniF2F test 26.5%, ProofNet 13.8%. lean-gym misjudged 21.1% of correct proofs vs 1.4% in LeanDojo. 33 new proofs found on miniF2F.
limits: One GPU-week model; older mathlib.
agent_relevance: A checker harness can itself be wrong 21% of the time. Test the verifier on known-good items before trusting its failures.

source: First et al. (2023) Baldur: whole-proof generation and repair
finding: Whole-proof generation then repair from the error message beats step-by-step search for Isabelle. Repair adds a little.
numbers: 6,336 Isabelle theorems: whole-proof 47.9% vs search-based 39.0%; repair adds 1.5%; Baldur plus Thor 65.7%, Thor alone 58.0%.
limits: Fine-tuned models, not prompting only. Repair gain is small.
agent_relevance: Models fix proofs after seeing the real error (G2) but repair rounds give small returns; combine different tools instead.

source: Thakur et al. (2024) COPRA in-context learning agent for formal proving
finding: Agent loop: GPT-4 proposes one tactic, the proof assistant runs it, error and state feed the next prompt, with backtracking and retrieved lemmas. No fine-tuning.
numbers: miniF2F-test Lean, 60 queries: few-shot GPT-4 13.52%; COPRA 26.63%; +retrieval 29.09%; +informal 29.92%; 100 queries 30.74%. No backtracking 24.59%. ReProver 25.00%. GPT-3.5 9.02%, CodeLlama 5.73%. Few-shot with 60 samples 15.98%.
limits: Needs GPT-4-class model; weaker models gain little.
agent_relevance: A working LLM agent loop on search with a hard checker. State feedback roughly doubles few-shot; backtracking is worth about 2 points.

finding: Hard undergraduate benchmark: 640 theorems in Lean 4 and Isabelle, 412 in Coq. Early 2024 systems solved almost nothing.
numbers: Lean 4: GPT-4 1/640, COPRA 1/640, ReProver 0/640. Isabelle: GPT-4 1/640, DSP 4/640, Sledgehammer 3/640. Coq: GPT-4 1/412, Tactician 0/412.
limits: GPT-4 only at pass@10; counts are tiny.
agent_relevance: Provers tuned on easy sets do not transfer to hard ones. Expect a big gap between easy and hard exact tasks.

finding: Whole-proof model with RL from proof-assistant feedback plus tree search with an intrinsic-reward bonus (RMaxTS). Chain-of-thought mode beat non-CoT.
numbers: miniF2F-test whole-proof 60.2% (V1: 50.0%), with RMaxTS 63.5%; pass@128 51.6%. ProofNet 25.3% with search. SFT raised pass@128 by about two thirds on miniF2F; RL gains held at large budgets.
limits: Training heavy. Tree search added about 3 points over whole-proof sampling.
agent_relevance: Natural-language planning before formal code helps. An exploration bonus is a cheap idea; the gain is small.

finding: A general model decomposes a problem into subgoals; subgoal proofs are recombined; then RL. CoT mode beat non-CoT but used about 9 times the tokens.
numbers: miniF2F-test 82.4% pass@32, 88.9% pass@8192 (217/244). PutnamBench 47/658. AIME 24-25 (15 problems): 6 solved formally vs 8 by DeepSeek-V3 majority vote informally. 7B CoT 68.85% at pass@32. Output tokens 671B: non-CoT 761.8 vs CoT 6751.9.
limits: Large sampling budgets; formal still trails informal on AIME.
agent_relevance: Subgoal lists written by a strong model and checked one by one are the core of a subgoal library. Track token cost.

finding: 1.64M formal statements made by an LLM translating Numina problems; successive provers add solved proofs. SFT alone beat the RL prover V1.5.
numbers: miniF2F 57.6% pass@32 (7.6 above DeepSeek V1.5). PutnamBench 7 problems at pass@512. Over 800K statements solved. RL/DPO took it past 60%.
limits: Statement translation quality had to be managed.
agent_relevance: Expert iteration works because the checker filters data; the same filter can decide which sub-proofs enter a library.

finding: Verifier-guided self-correction: Lean error text is fed back for rounds of revision. Model averaging restores diversity lost in late training.
numbers: 32B: miniF2F 88.1% pass@32, 90.4% with 2 correction rounds. 8B: 84.6% pass@32, above the 671B DeepSeek-Prover-V2. PutnamBench 86 at pass@184. Self-correction adds about 2 points.
limits: Pass@1 rose while pass@N fell in late training until averaging; self-correction budget 40,000 tokens.
agent_relevance: Revising from real compiler output is the supported kind of reflection (G2). The gain is about 2 points, not large.

finding: RL on a structured formal reasoning pattern that interleaves thought and Lean code. Scales with model size, unlike earlier provers.
numbers: miniF2F-test 80.7% at pass@8192. A 7B distilled version scored 63.1% at pass@32 (from the DeepSeek-V2 comparison table).
limits: Technical report of a preview model; budgets differ across compared systems.
agent_relevance: Thought then checked tactic works. Same shape as a step loop where a program judges each step.

finding: Train the model to write an informal thought before each tactic. Thoughts built backward from known good tactics, then expert iteration with the Lean checker.
numbers: miniF2F-test Pass@64 43.4% to 46.3%.
limits: About 3 points; needs training; thoughts are made after the fact, so faithfulness is untested.
agent_relevance: Written thoughts help the next step but do not prove why. Keep the checker as judge.

finding: Runs LLM inference inside Lean so a human or an automated tactic can call it. Compared with the rule-based AESOP search on a textbook.
numbers: Mathematics in Lean: 2.08 manual steps needed with Copilot vs 3.86 with AESOP; 74.2% of steps automated vs 40.1% (85% better).
limits: Textbook-level exercises.
agent_relevance: LLM as one tactic inside a rule-based tool, called when rules stall. A clean tool-use pattern.

finding: Lifelong-learning prover over many Lean repositories, with curriculum order and a growing database of knowledge.
numbers: Proved 155 theorems across 23 repositories that had no formal proofs before; beat a static baseline.
limits: Training based; per-baseline gaps were not read.
agent_relevance: Easy-first ordering plus a growing store of solved lemmas parallels a subgoal library.

finding: Agent loop with four parts: general informal reasoner, Lean prover, verifier, retriever. When the prover fails, the reasoner splits the problem into subgoals, recursively.
numbers: miniF2F 99.2%. PutnamBench 462/660 (70.0%) vs Seed-Prover 50.4%. Gemini 2.5 Pro alone at pass@16384: 49.1% on miniF2F. Hilbert lifted DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B non-CoT by 35.4 points (to 96.7%).
limits: Depends on strong informal models (Gemini 2.5, gpt-oss-120b); budgets: up to 4 sketch attempts, 6 shallow passes.
agent_relevance: Closest to our design: prose model plans and splits, checker verifies, failure triggers decomposition (G1: split only on failure).

finding: Lemma-style whole-proof model that refines from Lean feedback, proved lemmas and self-summaries. Three test-time settings: light, medium, heavy.
numbers: Past IMO 121/155 (78.1%). IMO 2025 5/6 after the contest (4/6 in time). miniF2F 99.6%. PutnamBench light 201/657, medium 331/657 (prior best 86). CombiBench 30/100. MiniCTX-v2 81.8% vs o4-mini 44.3% (Pass@8).
limits: Very large compute; combinatorics still weak; one miniF2F item unsolved.
agent_relevance: More test-time search on a hard checker keeps paying (201 to 331). Use a budget knob that grows only on failure.

finding: The LLM only translates text to first-order logic; the prover Prover9 does the inference. Failure modes differ from chain-of-thought failure modes.
numbers: ProofWriter balanced subset: GPT-4 + LINC 98.3%, GPT-3.5 + LINC 96.4%. StarCoder+ with LINC beat GPT-3.5 CoT by 38 points and GPT-4 CoT by 10. FOLIO GPT-4: CoT 75.3% vs LINC 72.5% (McNemar p=0.58, no difference). FOL syntax errors: 38% StarCoder+, 24% GPT-3.5, 13% GPT-4.
limits: FOLIO is natural text and loses implicit facts (for example that Harry is a person). ProofWriter is synthetic and easy to formalise.
agent_relevance: Offloaded deduction beats prose when text is clean; on messy text translation is the failure. The two methods fail differently, so using both gives a real check (G4).

finding: LLM formalises, a symbolic solver reasons, and solver error messages drive a refine step. Falls back to CoT when the logic cannot run.
numbers: Average gain +39.2 over standard and +18.4 over CoT (GPT-3.5). FOLIO with GPT-4: standard 69.11, CoT 70.58, Logic-LM 78.92. Executable rate: FOLIO GPT-4 79.9%, AR-LSAT GPT-4 32.6% (39.8% after refinement). Refinement raised executable rate by 5.01 points on average.
limits: Executable rate is low on hard sets; accuracy of the executable cases is high.
agent_relevance: Solver error text is a free, honest signal (G2). Plan a fallback path for when formalisation fails.

finding: LLM writes declarative constraints; a SAT/SMT solver finds the answer. The solver can report unsatisfiable or ambiguous specs, which lets the system abstain.
numbers: code-davinci-002 greedy: GSM-SYS 69.4 vs CoT 46.5 vs program-aided 43.4; CLUTRR 68.3 vs 40.8; ProofWriter 99.7 vs 80.1; LSAT 35.0 vs 23.5; BoardGameQA 79.4. New best LSAT 37.4% (from 30.9%), BoardgameQA 80.7% (from 73.9%). Selective prediction on GSM-SYS: 77% vs 45% accuracy at equal coverage.
limits: On plain GSM, program-aided is comparable (72.7 vs 71.8). Older Codex model.
agent_relevance: Declarative spec plus solver beats step-by-step code when search is the problem. UNSAT and AMBIG results are exact stop signals.

source: Jiang et al. (2023) DSP: classic prover baselines
finding: The classic hammer Sledgehammer plus hand heuristics already proves a fifth of miniF2F-test. LLM sketch guidance doubled it.
numbers: Test: Sledgehammer 10.4%, with heuristics 20.9%; Thor 29.9%; Thor + expert iteration 35.2%; DSP 39.3%. Valid: Sledgehammer 9.9%, heuristics 18.0%, Thor 28.3%, Thor+EI 37.3%, DSP 42.6%.
limits: Row alignment recovered from text extraction; read as approximate.
agent_relevance: Keep symbolic search tools and use the LLM to aim them (premise choice, sketch), not to replace them.

source: Tsoukalas et al. (2024) PutnamBench: failure modes
finding: GPT-4 wrote Lean 3 syntax even when told to use Lean 4. The one problem solved in both Lean and Coq (Putnam 1988 B1) was not solved in Isabelle by any method.
numbers: At most 1 to 4 of 640 solved per method.
limits: Tiny counts make method comparison weak.
agent_relevance: Check output format against the checker before calling a thought wrong; some failures are syntax, not reasoning.

source: ByteDance Seed (2025) Seed-Prover: subject and difficulty breakdown
finding: Even the strongest prover is uneven by subject. Formal difficulty differs from informal difficulty.
numbers: IMO easy 47/55, medium 47/56, hard 27/44. Algebra 72/85, number theory 42/55, combinatorics 7/14. Easy AMC items were hard to formalise (Vieta, root counting).
limits: Single system; small combinatorics count.
agent_relevance: Route by subject: for counting and combinatorics prefer exhaustive checking by code over a theorem prover.

source: Xin et al. (2024) DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5: budget comparison
finding: With 3,200 whole-proof samples the model matched the earlier best tree search that used far more search.
numbers: V1.5-RL at 3200 samples 54.9% vs InternLM2-StepProver 64 x 3200 tree searches 54.5%. ProofNet at 3200: 21.7% vs 18.1% before.
limits: Different training data across systems.
agent_relevance: A broad cheap sample plus checker can match deep search. Test best-of-N with a checker before building search.
